history: A diploma was originally folded in two. Greek diploun means ‘to double, to fold’, and a díplōma was a sheet folded over, the way an official letter or a travel permit was made. Latin borrowed it for a document issued by an authority, such as the licence which let a messenger use the imperial post. Medieval scholars used it for charters, the documents of a king or a bishop. Only later did diploma settle on its modern sense: a certificate of studies. In Italy il diploma usually means the high school certificate, as in diploma di maturità, and it is a standard requirement for many jobs. Una laurea is the university degree. English diplomat comes from the same word through French.
historyEinfach: Diploma comes from a Greek word for ‘a paper folded in two’. In Latin it meant an official letter. In Italy il diploma is mostly the certificate from the end of high school. A university degree is called una laurea. English diplomat comes from the same word.
